title: First Practical Experiences Integrating Quantum Computers with HPC Resources: A Case Study With a 20-qubit Superconducting Quantum Computer
problem: Integrating quantum computers with traditional HPC systems presents facility, operational, and training challenges
method: Case study of 20-qubit superconducting quantum computer integration at Leibniz Supercomputing Centre

title: AutoRFM: Scaling Low-Cost in-DRAM Trackers to Ultra-Low Rowhammer Thresholds
problem: In-DRAM Rowhammer mitigation using the DDR5 Refresh Management (RFM) command stalls the entire DRAM bank for 200-400ns per invocation; at ultra-low Rowhammer thresholds (sub-100), the required RFM frequency causes up to 33% performance slowdown with existing low-cost trackers such as MINT.
method: AutoRFM performs transparent RFM at the subarray granularity rather than the full bank level: it targets only one subarray at a time for mitigation while all other subarrays continue to service requests uninterrupted. If an activation request arrives for the subarray currently under mitigation, the DRAM chip issues an ALERT signal to the Memory Controller to retry after a bounded 200ns wait. Randomized Memory Mapping breaks spatial correlation between consecutive bank accesses to prevent repeated targeting of the same subarray. A Fractal Mitigation Algorithm handles transitive Rowhammer attacks (e.g., Half-Double) without recursive same-subarray mitigations. The design is evaluated with SPEC, GAP, and stream workloads.

title: 10.4 A 2- TRX IR-UWB Transceiver with Shared Antennas Supporting Channels 5 to 12 in Compliance with IEEE 802.15.4/4z Standards
problem: IR-UWB transceivers must support multiple channels (5-12) to reduce interference in crowded 6GHz spectrum while minimizing cost through antenna sharing, but previous integrated RF switches suffer high insertion loss degrading receiver sensitivity.
method: Fully integrated 2-TRX IR-UWB transceiver with multi-channel support (channels 5-12), using integrated CMOS RF switches optimized to reduce insertion loss while supporting shared TX/RX antenna architecture per IEEE 802.15.4/4z.

title: Layer-Specific Hardware Pooling Designs for CNN Accelerators
problem: CNN accelerator design typically uses uniform pooling (e.g., max pooling only), but different layers may benefit from different pooling strategies.
method: Design-space exploration of combinatorial pooling techniques: combinations of Max pooling with deviation-based methods (AAD, BWAD, AMD) across different CNN layers. Evaluated on AlexNet, UNet, VGG-16. FPGA synthesis on Xilinx Zedboard; ASIC synthesis in Cadence 45nm.

title: Compute4Biology: Taking Stock of High Performance Computing Needs for Foundation Models in Biological Sciences
problem: Foundation models are transforming biological sciences, but their computational needs are highly diverse across domains (genomics, proteomics, chemistry). There is no systematic understanding of HPC requirements or co-design principles for biological AI workloads.
method: Systematic cross-domain analysis of foundation models in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, chemistry, and biomedical literature. Characterizes computational bottlenecks, I/O patterns, memory requirements, and compute kernels for each domain.

title: EQSIM Agent: A Conversational AI for Interactive Exploration of Large-scale Earthquake Simulation Data
problem: Large-scale earthquake simulations produce massive datasets that are difficult to explore; researchers lack specialized knowledge or programming skills to extract insights.
method: LLM-based conversational agent (EQSIM Agent) for interactive data exploration. Features natural language querying, vision-based waveform similarity search, and RAG system for literature integration.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper HP-MDR: High-performance and Portable Data Refactoring and Progressive Retrieval with Advanced GPUs
problem: Reproducibility of GPU-accelerated data refactoring requires independent artifact evaluation.
method: Artifact evaluation of SC25 paper 'HP-MDR' by Podhorszki et al., assessing experimental setup and result reproducibility.

title: ShadowLoad: Injecting State into Hardware Prefetchers
problem: Hardware prefetchers in modern CPUs maintain internal state (e.g., stride tables, stream detectors) that persists across security boundaries, and prior work showed this state leaks information across processes, user/kernel space, and trusted execution environments (TEEs). This paper extends the threat by demonstrating that an attacker can actively inject crafted state into a victim's prefetcher, turning it into a covert communication channel or an amplification primitive.
method: ShadowLoad crafts memory access sequences that train the hardware prefetcher's internal prediction structures (stride tables, stream buffers) to a desired state from an unprivileged attacker context. When the victim process subsequently executes, the pre-injected prefetcher state causes speculative prefetches that alter the victim's cache state or execution timing, enabling state injection across process, user-kernel, and TEE boundaries. The technique exploits the fact that prefetcher state is not flushed or partitioned at privilege transitions on affected CPUs.

title: Multi-Object Detection Through Meta-Training in Resource-Constrained UAV-Based Surveillance Applications
problem: Object detection in UAV surveillance requires real-time performance on resource-constrained edge devices. Domain variation (nighttime, crowds, weather, small objects) degrades detection accuracy, and standard models trained on limited domains generalize poorly to real-world conditions.
method: Meta-training framework for domain generalization (adaptation): YOLO models trained iteratively across diverse domains (nighttime, crowds, sunny weather, small objects) using gradient descent-based optimization. Transfer learning enables model to learn domain-adaptive features. Multiple YOLO configurations and public/custom datasets tested.

title: Embracing Imbalance: Dynamic Load Shifting among Microservice Containers in Shared Clusters
problem: Containers within the same microservice deployed in large shared clusters experience temporal and spatial performance imbalance due to resource contention; standard load-balancing policies assume homogeneous container performance and respond with over-provisioning, wasting resources while still frequently violating SLAs.
method: The paper proposes dynamic load shifting, a system that continuously monitors per-container performance metrics (latency, throughput) to detect imbalance and dynamically steers incoming requests toward higher-performing containers within the same microservice. Rather than treating imbalance as a problem to eliminate through uniform scheduling, the system embraces it by exploiting performance heterogeneity: hot containers receive fewer requests and cool containers receive more, allowing the cluster to extract more useful work without additional provisioning. The approach integrates with existing cluster schedulers and load balancers.

title: An Asynchronous 160×90 Flash LiDAR Sensor with Dynamic Frame Rates of 5 to 250fps Based on Pixelwise ToF Validation via a Background-Light-Adaptive Threshold
problem: Flash LiDAR sensors require large on-chip histogramming time-to-digital converters (hTDC) for time-correlated single-photon counting, constrained by physical size and impacting spatial resolution; frame-based sensors suffer suboptimal frame rates tied to worst-case pixel SNR, and background light intensity severely degrades conventional designs.
method: Asynchronous event-driven readout scheme with pixelwise ToF validation and background-light-adaptive threshold dynamically adjusts pixel sensitivity and event rate control. On-chip histogramming with intelligent pixel-level filtering enables 5–250fps dynamic frame rates. Architecture combines time-gated photon counting with spiking neuron-like event generation and integrated control logic for on-chip sensitivity adaptation.

title: TENSORMD: Accelerating Molecular Dynamics with a High-Performance Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
problem: Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) suffer from suboptimal performance when using general-purpose ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) because these frameworks are not optimized for the computational patterns and diversity of HPC+AI workloads.
method: TensorMD is a custom MLIP implementation decoupled from existing ML tools, enabling domain-specific optimizations tailored to the computational patterns of molecular dynamics. The approach identifies optimization opportunities unique to HPC+AI that general frameworks cannot exploit.

title: Scaling Hybrid Quantum-HPC Applications with the Quantum Framework
problem: Hybrid Q-HPC workflows must select best simulator for each circuit type; no single simulator optimal for all
method: Extended Quantum Framework (QFw) integrating Qiskit Aer, NWQ-Sim, QTensor, TN-QVM (local) and IonQ (cloud) under unified interface

title: OpenSHMEM MLIR: A Dialect for Compile-Time Optimization of One-Sided Communications
problem: Communication is a growing bottleneck in HPC, but mainstream compilers lose communication intent through opaque runtime calls. OpenSHMEM one-sided PGAS model has rich semantics but they are not preserved for compiler optimization.
method: Develop OpenSHMEM dialect for MLIR that preserves one-sided communication, symmetric memory, and team/context structures as first-class IR constructs. Integrate with existing MLIR/LLVM optimization passes. Demonstrate four specific transformations.

title: 35.2 A Spatial-Domain Compressive-Sensing Photoacoustic Imager with Matrix-Multiplying SAR ADC
problem: Wearable deep-tissue photoacoustic (PA) imaging requires low-power, compact receive architecture with integrated data compression for real-time streaming and long-term monitoring, but PA signals are 10x smaller than ultrasound due to optical excitation inefficiency.
method: A spatial-domain compressive-sensing receiver architecture with matrix-multiplying SAR ADC performs simultaneous signal acquisition and compression at the sensor level. The SAR ADC computes matrix-vector products during conversion, implementing spatial sampling and measurement in hardware. Optimized for PA's low signal amplitude by tuning gain, bandwidth, and noise characteristics.

title: 10.3 A D-Band 2D-Scalable 4×4 Active Reflective Relay with Orthogonally Polarized on-Chip TX/RX Antennas and in-Front-End Common-Centroid Fast Azimuth/Elevation Angle-of-Arrival Detection
problem: mm-Wave and sub-THz NLOS links require reflective relay arrays to overcome line-of-sight (LOS) blockage, but existing relays operate open-loop without on-the-fly angle-of-arrival (AoA) detection; prior AoA methods either require lossy down-/up-mixers, continuously tunable phase shifters with stability concerns, or narrow AoA range.
method: A 4×4 D-band active reflective relay integrates orthogonally polarized TX/RX on-chip antennas and implements in-front-end common-centroid fast AoA detection (both azimuth and elevation). The relay detects incident beam angles and steers the output beam adaptively without requiring lossy mixers or tunable phase shifter loops.
